I do too, but that's not the question. Handling yourself in a scuffle isn't going to be any help if your bike is stolen while you're somewhere else.

My strategies are:

1. Remove the Opportunity for Theft—Try not to leave the bike outside if at all possible. Easier said than done.

2. Security Through Obscurity—Bikes that look cheap or generic are less likely to be stolen.

3. Lock Through Seat Tube & Rear Tire—There's a saying that 'locks only keep out honest people,' but it will at least slow down the bike thief, or make them think about choosing an easier target.

Bike thieves are an unfortunate reality, and in my experience, they're not one that the police really care to stop. I went out to buy a bike off of Craigslist last weekend, and when I met the guy, he knew nothing about the bike. This was a very nice road bike, and typically not something you chance into owning. The seller (picture a typical shady character) kept saying things like "I've only had it a week" and "My friend gave it to me." Obviously, I didn't buy the bike. I tried checking in with the police afterward to see if they had a report of that make/model/year of bike being stolen, or had reports in the past about this guy stealing bikes, etc. They completely blew me off, and were extremely rude about it to boot. Moral of the story, don't trust the police to care about stolen bikes, it's up to you to keep your property safe!

I've been watching Craigslist and local forums to see if anything relevant pops up—it was a black, 54cm, 2006 Specialized Allez Elite with an upgraded wheelset, upgraded compact crank, and a nice computer, if anyone is missing it by chance. Denver area.
